node.title: E1 pure-cofactor common-prime associate router
node.closure: ideal factorization, AM-GM reduction, and exact conductor-256 unit-basis theorem
node.statement: At one fixed prize N=256 reduction root, every collision of absolute norm 2^mu p has principal ideal P_r(1-zeta)^mu. Dividing by the ramified factor gives a generator of P_r, so every two pure-cofactor collisions are normalized unit associates. Fixed-cofactor associates have explicit unit/inverse coefficient boxes and, modulo 256 shifts/signs, inject into an exact AM-GM body in the full rank-63 unit log lattice. That lattice has an explicit 63-circular-unit integer basis, and the exact maximum-weight profile target is at most 367 torsion orbits.
node.notes: ANALYTIC AGGREGATE ROUTER 2026-07-29: the current profile-(3,6,S=18) residue has cofactors 2,4,8,16, with only the primitive m=16 support branch live. Cramer-Hadamard gives coefficient bounds 1006,503,251,125; the log body is ||lambda||_1<=2(D+sqrt(128D)), D=log(18^64/(2^mu p)). Miller's unconditional h+=1 theorem and Kummer-Sinnott identify the full lattice with 63 explicit circular units. Each orbit pays 128M_33(3,6) edges; 368 already exceed the complete edge budget. No orbit count, lower-profile payment, E1 image bound, or prize status movement follows.
